name: open-source-pattern-adoption-template
purpose: Record how high-signal open-source agent platform repositories can influence this platform without unsafe code copying, license drift, or architecture churn.

reader_guide.summary: Use this file before implementing structures inspired by trending or high-star open-source agent repositories.
how_to_read: Read platform_context first to understand the local design boundary.
Read source_repositories as provenance and adoption signals, not proof that a pattern must be copied.
Read pattern_candidates to see reusable structures found across repositories.
Read language_runtime_options, architecture_options, and folder_structure_options before changing code.
Read clone_import_policy before cloning or importing any source code.
Read adoption_decisions to see what is adopted now, trialed, or kept as reference only.
update_triggers: A new source repository is used as implementation evidence.
A direct code import, clone, dependency install, or hybrid module is proposed.
The platform source structure changes in response to open-source patterns.
A repository license, activity, or architecture signal changes materially.

structure_rules.rule: Stars, social activity, comments, and trend ranking are adoption or discovery signals only; implementation decisions require source inspection, license posture, local fit, and validation.
structure_rules.reason: Popularity can expose useful patterns but cannot prove correctness or compatibility.

structure_rules.rule: Prefer native Python validators and local adapter contracts before importing third-party framework code.
structure_rules.reason: The current platform is a Python-first governance and evaluation layer with stable local interfaces.

structure_rules.rule: Direct code import requires explicit permission plus license review, pinned commit, source provenance, attribution, tests, rollback, and human checkpoint.
structure_rules.reason: Copying code without these gates creates legal, maintenance, and provenance risk.

structure_rules.rule: Hybrid modules may use another language only behind a build boundary and versioned interface contract.
structure_rules.reason: Other runtimes can be useful for provider SDKs, browser UI, or sandboxed execution, but they need isolated builds and rollback.

field_guide.meaning: Local platform facts that constrain which open-source patterns are appropriate.
Repositories inspected for structure patterns, with license posture and adoption-signal caveats.
Reusable structure patterns extracted from source repositories.
Compared implementation runtimes, including Python and hybrid alternatives.
Compared folder layouts and ownership semantics before creating or reshaping source folders.
Rules for cloning repositories and importing external code.
Boundary and build contract for using other languages as isolated platform modules.
Accepted, trialed, reference-only, deferred, or rejected pattern decisions.
Commands that must pass before the plan can guide implementation.

platform_context: This platform currently uses Python-first deterministic validators, self-documenting JSON configs, local CLI commands, and durable history records to govern agent work. Open-source repositories can supply structural patterns, but copied framework code, new dependencies, and other-language modules must stay behind explicit adapter, build, license, provenance, validation, and rollback gates.

source_repositories.name: LangGraph
source_repositories.adoption_signal_role: High-star active repository used as a structure signal; stars are not proof of local fit.
useful_patterns: Graph and state contracts are separated from persistence adapters.
Checkpoint providers are split into dedicated modules.
Python and JavaScript SDK surfaces are separated from core graph implementation.
source_repositories.caveats: Adopt patterns through local contracts; do not add LangGraph as a dependency unless a specific workflow requires it and install review is recorded.

source_repositories.name: OpenAI Agents Python
source_repositories.adoption_signal_role: Official-source repository and active adoption signal for agent runtime structure.
useful_patterns: Agent definition, run state, guardrails, handoffs, sandboxing, and tracing are separated.
Runtime behavior is easier to evaluate when lifecycle, tool, and guardrail surfaces are distinct.
source_repositories.caveats: Use the module split as an architecture reference; avoid importing runtime code into governance validators.

source_repositories.name: Pydantic AI
useful_patterns: Typed tools, toolsets, providers, models, and MCP boundaries are separated.
Schema-first interfaces make tool execution easier to validate.
source_repositories.caveats: Typing patterns fit the platform, but direct dependency adoption still needs install and compatibility review.

source_repositories.name: CrewAI
source_repositories.adoption_signal_role: High-star Python multi-agent repository used as an orchestration concept signal.
useful_patterns: Separate crew and flow concepts can inform agent orchestration planning.
Project-level docs and scripts reinforce install and validation discipline.
source_repositories.caveats: Repository path conventions differ from this platform; use as conceptual reference unless a deeper implementation review is completed.

source_repositories.name: Semantic Kernel
source_repositories.adoption_signal_role: Multi-language agent framework signal for plugin, kernel, and adapter boundaries.
useful_patterns: Kernel and plugin concepts can inform local capability boundaries.
A mature non-Python ecosystem can inform hybrid module decisions without forcing a runtime change.
source_repositories.caveats: This slice did not deeply inspect source folders; use only as broad architecture signal until deeper review.

source_repositories.name: Dify
source_repositories.adoption_signal_role: Very high-star productized platform signal; reference-only until license posture is cleared.
useful_patterns: Productized monorepo separates API, web, CLI, agent package, SDKs, Docker, and end-to-end tests.
The split is useful when platform-desktop-app or external API surfaces mature.
source_repositories.caveats: GitHub metadata reported non-standard or unclear license status in this search pass; do not copy code without a license review.

source_repositories.name: OpenHands
source_repositories.adoption_signal_role: High-star software-agent platform signal for app server and runtime boundaries.
useful_patterns: Separate app-server, server/runtime, and analytics concerns.
Sandbox and execution boundaries are relevant to future agent execution modules.
source_repositories.caveats: License posture must be reviewed before direct code import; this plan uses it as reference only.

source_repositories.name: Mastra
source_repositories.adoption_signal_role: Modern TypeScript agent platform signal for modular package boundaries.
useful_patterns: Capability modules are split by agent, workflow, tool, storage, telemetry, evals, server, worker, and workspace.
TypeScript modules are plausible hybrid candidates for provider SDK and UI-facing packages.
source_repositories.caveats: Use as reference only until license and dependency review are complete.

source_repositories.name: Vercel AI SDK
source_repositories.adoption_signal_role: Provider package split signal for AI SDK integration patterns.
useful_patterns: Provider contracts and provider implementations are separated into packages.
Framework-specific UI bindings are separated from provider utilities.
source_repositories.caveats: Use the package split as a structure reference; direct import or dependency adoption needs license and install review.

pattern_candidates.name: State and checkpoint adapter contract
pattern_candidates.applicability: Useful when the platform stores task state, agent run state, resumable plans, or evaluation checkpoints.
pattern_candidates.implementation_surface: Future native Python contracts under agent_platform.memory, agent_platform.orchestration, or agent_platform.oss validation plans.
pattern_candidates.risks: Premature persistence abstraction can add complexity before a concrete stateful runtime exists.
pattern_candidates.evidence: LangGraph separates graph behavior from checkpoint modules and provider-specific persistence packages.

pattern_candidates.name: Run lifecycle, guardrail, handoff, sandbox, and tracing separation
pattern_candidates.applicability: Fits the platform's evaluator-first approach because lifecycle, guardrails, handoffs, sandboxing, and tracing can be validated independently.
pattern_candidates.implementation_surface: Native Python validators and future runtime interfaces before any third-party runtime adoption.
pattern_candidates.risks: Too many modules can fragment a small runtime; adopt only where the validation surface is real.
pattern_candidates.evidence: OpenAI Agents Python exposes separate modules for run state, guardrails, handoffs, sandboxing, and tracing.

pattern_candidates.name: Typed tool and provider contract
pattern_candidates.applicability: Useful for improving user AI ability by making tools, providers, and model interfaces explicit, inspectable, and testable.
pattern_candidates.implementation_surface: Future adapter contracts in agent_platform.adapters and config validators for tool/provider schemas.
pattern_candidates.risks: Provider-specific abstractions can leak into core models if adapter boundaries are weak.
pattern_candidates.evidence: Pydantic AI separates tools, toolsets, models, providers, and MCP; Vercel AI separates provider packages from framework bindings.

pattern_candidates.name: Productized monorepo split across API, web, CLI, agent package, SDK, and tests
pattern_candidates.applicability: Useful when this platform grows from repository governance into installable software, API, UI, SDK, and end-to-end workflows.
pattern_candidates.implementation_surface: Reference for future platform-desktop-app and agent-platform package boundaries, not current source code copying.
pattern_candidates.risks: Adopting a productized split too early would overbuild the repository.
pattern_candidates.evidence: Dify and Mastra show explicit API/web/CLI/package/SDK/runtime/test separation.

pattern_candidates.name: Sandboxed runtime boundary
pattern_candidates.applicability: Relevant when agent execution moves beyond validators into subprocesses, browser automation, file mutation, or external CLI control.
pattern_candidates.implementation_surface: Future resource guard, CLI adapter, and runtime policy checks.
pattern_candidates.risks: Sandboxing can create false confidence unless permissions, cleanup, and observability are measured.
pattern_candidates.evidence: OpenHands and OpenAI Agents Python expose runtime/sandbox-oriented boundaries.

pattern_candidates.name: Hybrid provider sidecar boundary
pattern_candidates.applicability: Useful when a TypeScript, C#, Rust, or Go ecosystem has materially better provider SDK, UI binding, sandbox, or performance properties than Python.
pattern_candidates.implementation_surface: Separate module or package with versioned JSON/stdio/HTTP adapter and independent build command.
pattern_candidates.risks: Multiple runtimes increase installation, dependency, build, and rollback complexity.
pattern_candidates.evidence: Semantic Kernel is a mature non-Python framework; Vercel AI and Mastra show TypeScript provider and platform module splits.

language_runtime_options.use_when: Implement deterministic governance, planning, research-readiness, and OSS adoption validators in the current agent-platform package.
language_runtime_options.tradeoffs: Best fit for the current codebase and tests; not always best for browser UI, provider SDK breadth, or high-performance sandboxing.
language_runtime_options.tooling: argparse, dataclasses, JSON configs, unittest, PYTHONPATH=src.
language_runtime_options.project_boundary_fit: Selected because agent-platform is already Python-first and this task is a validator/config capability.

language_runtime_options.use_when: Build provider SDK adapters, UI-facing packages, web views, or framework-specific bindings where the TypeScript ecosystem is stronger.
language_runtime_options.tradeoffs: Requires npm lockfiles, separate build, package boundary, and adapter contract.
language_runtime_options.tooling: npm, TypeScript compiler, package-level tests, JSON-over-stdio or HTTP adapter.
language_runtime_options.project_boundary_fit: Allowed only behind a hybrid module boundary or inside platform-desktop-app/web-facing packages.

language_runtime_options.use_when: Build a measured sandbox, file watcher, CLI supervisor, or high-throughput sidecar where safety or performance justifies another runtime.
language_runtime_options.tradeoffs: More reliable binaries may reduce runtime overhead but increase build, signing, cross-platform, and rollback complexity.
language_runtime_options.tooling: cargo or go test/build plus adapter smoke tests.
language_runtime_options.project_boundary_fit: Allowed only for a separately owned module with documented artifact contract.

language_runtime_options.use_when: A .NET plugin or kernel ecosystem capability is clearly superior and can run as an isolated service or CLI.
language_runtime_options.tradeoffs: Adds .NET runtime requirements and a separate package lifecycle.
language_runtime_options.tooling: dotnet build/test and versioned adapter contract.
language_runtime_options.project_boundary_fit: Reference-only for now; no .NET module is selected for this implementation slice.

architecture_options.name: Extend existing OSS validation layer
architecture_options.fit: Adds a deterministic pattern adoption gate under agent_platform.oss without changing runtime ownership.
architecture_options.tradeoffs: Does not copy external functionality directly, but creates a safer path for future direct imports or hybrid modules.

architecture_options.name: Clone and adapt a full open-source framework
architecture_options.fit: Could rapidly expose features from one framework if license, architecture, and implementation fit are already proven.
architecture_options.tradeoffs: High provenance, license, maintenance, integration, and lock-in risk; too broad for this request without a specific feature target.

architecture_options.name: Build a separate hybrid sidecar module
architecture_options.fit: Appropriate for provider SDK, UI, sandbox, or performance-sensitive functions that are materially better outside Python.
architecture_options.tradeoffs: Requires separate build, dependency audit, artifact contract, and rollback.
architecture_options.decision: trial as future option, not implemented in this slice

architecture_options.name: Document patterns without validator support
architecture_options.tradeoffs: Too easy to skip during future implementation; lacks close-out enforcement.
architecture_options.decision: rejected because the user requested implementation without omissions

folder_structure_options.name: Existing OSS module and open-source configs
folder_structure_options.semantics: Keep source under agent-platform/src/agent_platform/oss, templates under agent-platform/configs/open-source, tests under agent-platform/tests.
folder_structure_options.tradeoffs: Smallest durable path; reinforces that this is an OSS adoption gate rather than a new platform product.

folder_structure_options.name: New root project for OSS pattern lab
folder_structure_options.semantics: A separate project could clone, compare, and prototype external frameworks independently.
folder_structure_options.tradeoffs: Useful for a future experiment, but too much ownership overhead for a validator and policy gate.

folder_structure_options.name: Blend OSS adoption into orchestration modules
folder_structure_options.semantics: Place pattern decisions near agent orchestration validators.
folder_structure_options.tradeoffs: Would blur open-source provenance rules with orchestration contracts.
folder_structure_options.decision: rejected because OSS provenance should remain explicit

allowed_clone_scopes: read-only source inspection for architecture comparison
temporary isolated clone under a documented research path
license review and provenance audit before any copied code enters durable source
disallowed_conditions: Repository license is unclear, restrictive, or incompatible.
No pinned commit or release is recorded.
Copied code would cross project boundaries without a migration plan.
The feature can be implemented cleanly as a local pattern without copying.
No rollback plan or validation command exists.

candidate_languages.use_when: Provider SDKs, UI bindings, or web-facing modules are better served by the JavaScript ecosystem.
candidate_languages.artifact_contract: Versioned JSON-over-stdio, HTTP, or package API contract with schema tests.
candidate_languages.risks: Separate dependency lockfile, install audit, and runtime failure modes.

candidate_languages.use_when: A sandbox, file watcher, or CLI supervisor needs low overhead and strong binary boundaries.
candidate_languages.artifact_contract: Versioned binary with explicit input/output schema and smoke tests.

candidate_languages.use_when: A simple cross-platform sidecar or process supervisor is easier to ship as a standalone binary.
candidate_languages.artifact_contract: Versioned binary or service with JSON input/output contract.
candidate_languages.risks: Additional module ownership and dependency audit burden.

candidate_languages.use_when: A Semantic Kernel style plugin or kernel service is justified by .NET ecosystem fit.
candidate_languages.artifact_contract: Versioned CLI or local service with JSON schema and health checks.

hybrid_module_plan.build_boundary: Hybrid code must live in its own owned module or project folder, build separately, and expose only a documented adapter contract to agent-platform.
hybrid_module_plan.interface_contract: Use versioned JSON schemas over stdio, HTTP, or a narrow package API; never let hybrid provider internals leak into agent_platform.core.
verification_commands: Run the hybrid module's own build command.
Run adapter contract tests from agent-platform.
Run PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests from agent-platform.
hybrid_module_plan.rollback_plan: Disable the adapter registration, remove the hybrid module dependency or build artifact, rerun platform tests, and keep the last passing native Python path as fallback.

adoption_decisions.rationale: The immediate platform need is not to copy agent framework code, but to separate evidence, guardrails, decisions, and validation so future adoption cannot skip safety gates.
implementation_steps: Add a deterministic validator for source repositories, patterns, language choices, architecture choices, folder choices, clone policy, hybrid plan, adoption decisions, and validation commands.
Expose the validator through the agent-platform CLI.
Add tests for passing plans, direct code import blocks, and hybrid module gates.
guardrails: No third-party framework dependency is installed in this slice.
No external source code is copied into durable source.
Direct code imports remain blocked unless explicit gates and human checkpoint are recorded.

adoption_decisions.rationale: Checkpoint adapter separation is likely useful for resumable work state, but the current implementation only needs a validator and future pattern record.
implementation_steps: Record the pattern as a trial candidate.
Require future state/checkpoint implementation to compare native persistence, SQLite/Postgres adapter, and external graph framework options.
guardrails: Do not add persistence abstractions until a concrete runtime or stateful workflow requires them.
Keep checkpoint providers behind local contracts.
validation_steps: Run check-oss-pattern-adoption after any future state/checkpoint plan update.

adoption_decisions.rationale: Typed provider and tool contracts directly improve user AI capability by making tools inspectable and verifiable, but implementation should happen in local adapters.
implementation_steps: Use the pattern to design future provider and tool adapter schemas.
Require schema validation before adapter activation.
guardrails: No provider SDK dependency is installed without installation audit.
Provider-specific behavior must not leak into core platform models.
validation_steps: Run adapter contract tests once adapter schemas are created.

adoption_decisions.rationale: The monorepo product split is useful for future platform-desktop-app and API/UI/SDK productization, but current implementation should stay scoped to agent-platform OSS governance.
Sandbox/runtime boundaries matter for future execution work, but this request does not launch long-running runtimes or subprocess orchestration.
Other-language modules can be the right fit for provider SDKs, UI, sandboxing, or performance, but they must be introduced as separate build artifacts with adapter contracts.
implementation_steps: Keep hybrid module support as a governed option in this plan.
Before creating a hybrid module, record language choice, build command, artifact contract, dependency audit, validation commands, and rollback plan.
guardrails: Do not create a hybrid module without a specific capability target and install/build audit.
Keep Python validator path as fallback.
validation_steps: Run check-oss-pattern-adoption and the future module's build/test commands before activation.
